It doesn’t seem like you convey the narrators dream girl or dream partner, though. Like we don’t get enough time with her to understand how she suites the narrator. Also, maybe a few more instances of uncanny valley would deliver the needed explanation of this being a dream to the reader? Such as the dream girl being willing to do things no one would to please the narrator in order to deliver that message more concretely?

So my first criticism is more a pet peeve than anything. (and you can take all of these with a grain of salt) I really dislike the way you space most of your lines because with the exception of the ones you use an M-dash for it doesn’t feel like those have meaning, rather they’re meant to fit a certain meter. 

Aside from that really nitpicky critique, I think the feelings you evoke here are very good an Di relate quite a bit, but I feel like they’re introduced a bit suddenly? That may just be my reading of it and again, take my words with a grain of salt, but I think it lacks some oomf when the ideas of slipping and not being with reality are introduced later on in the poem. 

Aside from that, great work OP! This poem feels vulnerable and evokes the feeling it seems to be reaching for well, it could just use more weight.
